text:
laura: Quick summary — production perf alert: noticed a reproducible cold-start hit-rate collapse on KV prefix cache when serving RAG workloads vs plain completions. p50 token latency fine, p99 token latency jumps ~30% under load.

sam: Seen the traces, looks like cache miss storms during conversation reconstructions. lots of unique cache keys for very similar prefixes.

mike: Do we have kernel switch correlation? e.g. different kernel chosen because sequence length spikes, causing batching to behave differently?

jenny: I ran a sampling job over last 24h. Findings: RAG prompts have high structured metadata (json blobs, source markers). Cache key fingerprinting currently includes the full prompt string + convo_id. That leads to high cardinality.

laura: exact numbers from the sample: completions hit-rate ~62%, chat (short convo) ~58%, RAG median hit-rate ~21%. Warm nodes recover to ~45% after prefix compaction but cold sessions stay low.

omar: Interesting. Kernel swap does show up in traces right before latency spikes — we flip to the long-context kernel at t=0 sometimes which reduces batching coalescing window. fewer concurrent tokens batched -> higher per-token cost.

sam: So two amplifiers: key fragmentation causing misses, then kernel choice making each miss more expensive.

mike: Agree. Also saw in logs that the KV cache prefetch is disabled for keys longer than 2k characters (we strip), but RAG prefixes often have nested JSON >2k so prefetch path is skipped.

jenny: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) canonicalize prompt keys (normalize whitespace, sort JSON fields for source metadata, remove ephemeral trace ids), 2) drop convo_id from key and replace with convo-fingerprint that only includes prefix-relevant fields, 3) extend prefetch length threshold to 8k behind a canary flag.

laura: Can we prototype canonicalization safely? Risk: might increase false positives (different prompts normalized to same key) — need evals.

omar: I ran a small offline diff: after canonicalization (whitespace collapse + JSON sort + trim ephemeral keys) hit-rate on sample RAG set jumped from 21% -> 53% with zero measurable quality regressions in loglikelihood probes.

sam: Nice. What about collisions? I want a hash prefix + length bucket in key to reduce accidental collisions. e.g. key = sha256(norm_prompt)[:24] + ":L" + str(len(norm_prompt))

mike: That plus keeping a small secondary fingerprint of the full original prompt (2 bytes) should make collisions astronomically unlikely.

jenny: Ops plan: implement normalization in canary branch on runtime nodes in us-west-2c, enable extended prefetch, instrument hit/miss + collision counters, collect 6h canary traces. Rollback if collision > 1e-5 or quality drift observed.

laura: Also add kernel selection telemetry to the canary: log kernel_id, seq_len, batch_coalescing_window_ms for each request so we can correlate.

omar: I patched a quick micro-benchmark: with normalized keys and extended prefetch the p99 token time on RAG decreases by ~28% in the canary simulated workload. batch sizes increased ~1.8x.

sam: Good. Edge case: structured output generation — we sometimes include system/protocol markers in prompts for schema-constrained responses. Normalization must not remove role tokens that change semantics.

mike: Agreed — normalization should whitelist role tokens: <system>, <assistant>, <user> remain exact, only free-form metadata fields get canonicalized.

jenny: I'll open the PR for the normalization library and the runtime flag today: PATCH 3582. Will include a small corpus of regression prompts and an automated quality check that compares top-3 token probabilities.

laura: Can we also add a short-lived route-level override so customers with strict determinism can opt out?

omar: yes, add a header x-rw-cache-normalize: off. We'll make sure not to affect Dedicated/private default unless customer opts in.

sam: Timeline: canary deploy tonight, collect 6-12h telemetry, then gradual rollout over 24h if stable. Postmortem to include root-cause analysis and cost impact delta.

mike: I'll prepare dashboards: cache hit-rate by workload tag (chat/completion/RAG), kernel-switch rate, p99 token latency, collision counter.

laura: Thanks. Last note — add a test that simulates long-context kernel borderline cases to ensure we don't flip kernels unnecessarily after normalization. We want batching win without unexpected kernel churn.

infra-bot: deploy-canary triggered: eng-runtime/canaries/normalize-kv-3582 -> us-west-2c nodes (3 replicas). Tracking ID: canary-3582-usrw.

jenny: ping me if you see collision counter > 0.0001 or quality drift.

laura: Great work team. We'll reconvene in 12h with canary metrics. :thumbsup:
